title: ר' יוחנן בן נורי

paragraphs: (1) In the Mishnah: Kilayim 6:1; Terumot 10:11; Challah 4:2; Eruvin 4:5 (45a); Rosh Hashanah 2:8, chapter 4 (received locator פ״ר), mishnayot 5, 6 (32a); Yevamot 14:1; Ketubbot 1:10; Nedarim 11:4; Bava Metzia 3:7; Eduyot 2:10; Chullin 9:2, 3; Bekhorot 6:6; Temurah 1:1 (7b); Keritot 3:7; Kelim 12:7, 11:3, 17:5, 14, 17, 30:2; Oholot 2:7, 6:7, 8:1, 12:1, 14:3; Negaim 10:1, 14:10; Parah 12:8; Mikvaot 7:1, 5; Tevul Yom 2:5, 6; Tohorot 8:6; Uktzin 3:5, 6.

(2) He was called ‘the peddlers’ basket’: Gittin 67; in Avot de-Rabbi Natan, end of chapter 18, ‘a basket of laws.’ He disputes with Rabban Gamliel over sanctifying the month: Rosh Hashanah 25a. He did not let Rabbi Yehoshua annul Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh’s words; see his entry. He decided the laws according to Rabban Gamliel: the chapter BaKol Mearvin, 41a. There, chapter 1, 11b, Rabbi Yehoshua went to him to learn Torah and called him ‘Rabbi.’ In the Tosefta, Terumot, chapter 6, Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah said: ‘An incident: Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah went to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri at Beit Shearim.’ In the Jerusalem Talmud, Terumot 8:6, Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah said: ‘An incident: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri went to my father, Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah, at Beit Sherei.’ In the Tosefta, Sukkah, chapter 2: ‘Rabbi said: Once I came with Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Tzadok to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri at Beit Shearim.’ Rabbi did not live in his time; it should be Rabban Gamliel, who is called simply Berabbi (Yuchasin, sequence of generations under Rabbi Tzadok). He was Rabbi Akiva’s colleague before Rabban Gamliel. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri told Rabbi Akiva: ‘How long will you feed people carcasses?’ Rabbi Akiva replied: ‘How long will you destroy Israel’s money?’ Bekhorot 40a. In Zevachim 6b: ‘Rabbi Akiva’s words; Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says’—this is how it should read, new Talmud edition. Arakhin 16b, Sifra, Kedoshim, and Sifrei, beginning of Devarim: ‘Many times Akiva was flogged on my account, because I would complain of him before Rabban Shimon Berabbi.’ In the new Talmud edition: Gamliel; so too Ein Yaakov, but without the word Berabbi. This means Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, who was called Berabbi, as above. ‘And he increased his love for me’ (Yuchasin, sequence of generations under Rabbi Akiva). Rabban Gamliel appointed him together with Rabbi Elazar ben Chisma to preside: Sifrei, Devarim, the section ‘And I charged your judges.’ But in Horayot 10a the reading is Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda and Rabbi Elazar Chisma; that is the primary reading (Yuchasin, sequence of generations under Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda). In Yoma 38a, an elder of the House of Avtinas handed him a scroll of ingredients. One who sees Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri in a dream should anticipate fear of sin (Avot de-Rabbi Natan, end of chapter 40).

(3) In Rabbi Eliezer the Great’s name: Kiddushin 39a. ‘I said to Rabbi Eliezer,’ and so forth. Rabbi Yose said: ‘I said to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, I wonder whether Rabbi Eliezer accepted your answer’: Tosefta, Kelim, chapter 6. And Rabbi E. ben Teradyon. Chilfa bar Agra transmitted in his name. Rabbi Chalafta, Rabbi Yose’s father, learned before him—or the reverse. Rabbi Yose said: ‘Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri came to Rabbi Chalafta and asked: What do you say about a pika [פיקה, a rounded fitting]? He replied: Impure. He said: I say so too, but Akiva declares it pure’: Tosefta, Kelim, chapter 8. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah went to him: Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah 1:1. Rabbi Yose HaGelili transmitted in his name. Rabbi Yose said: ‘An incident came before Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri’; Rabbi Yose also transmitted in his name. ‘Rabbi Yochanan said in Ben Azzai’s name’: Nazir 65a, end. Tosafot write that this is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, rather than Rabbi Yochanan the amora. If Tosafot’s necessary reason is how Rabbi Yochanan the amora could speak in Ben Azzai’s name, since Ben Azzai preceded him by much, you will find a counterexample: Rabbi Yochanan the amora spoke in the names of tannaim earlier than Ben Azzai. Examine it carefully there, and see there that Tosafot’s explanation does not seem right to me. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai learned with him.
